A company’s reporting system delivers hundreds of .csv files to an Amazon S3 bucket each day. The company must convert these files to Apache
Parquet format and must store the files in a transformed data bucket.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?
correctAnswer: Create an AWS Glue crawler to discover the data. Create an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to transform the data. Specify the transformed data bucket in the output step.
incorrectAnswers: Create an Amazon EMR cluster with Apache Spark installed. Write a Spark application to transform the data. Use EMR File System (EMRFS) to write files to the transformed data bucket.

A company has a serverless website with millions of objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company uses the S3 bucket as the origin for an
Amazon CloudFront distribution. The company did not set encryption on the S3 bucket before the objects were loaded. A solutions architect
needs to enable encryption for all existing objects and for all objects that are added to the S3 bucket in the future.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of effort?
correctAnswer: Turn on the default encryption settings for the S3 bucket. Use the S3 Inventory feature to create a .csv file that lists the unencrypted objects. Run an S3 Batch Operations job that uses the copy command to encrypt those objects.
incorrectAnswers: Create a new S3 bucket. Turn on the default encryption settings for the new S3 bucket. Download all existing objects to temporary local storage. Upload the objects to the new S3 bucket.

Create a new encryption key by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Change the settings on the S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS managed encryption keys (SSE-KMS). Turn on versioning for the S3 bucket.

Navigate to Amazon S3 in the AWS Management Console. Browse the S3 bucket's objects. Sort by the encryption field. Select each unencrypted object. Use the Modify button to apply default encryption settings to every unencrypted object in the S3 bucket.
explanation:
Default encryption applies only to new objects. S3 Inventory reports each object's encryption status, and an S3 Batch Operations Copy job re-writes the existing objects in place so they become encrypted, at scale and with no download. Note: since January 2023 S3 applies SSE-S3 to all new uploads by default, but objects stored earlier remain unencrypted until copied.

Source: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/storage/encrypting-objects-with-amazon-s3-batch-operations/

factChecks.explanation: Keyed answer (new bucket, download everything locally, re-upload millions of objects) is the MOST effort, not least, and requires repointing CloudFront. A solutions architect is designing a new API using Amazon API Gateway that will receive requests from users. The volume of requests is highly
variable; several hours can pass without receiving a single request. The data processing will take place asynchronously, but should be completed
within a few seconds after a request is made.

correctAnswer: An AWS Lambda function
incorrectAnswers: An AWS Glue job
A containerized service hosted in Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
A containerized service hosted in Amazon ECS with Amazon EC2
explanation:
Lambda is invoked by API Gateway, runs in seconds, and charges only for execution time, so idle hours cost nothing. EKS or ECS on EC2 have always-on compute cost, and Glue jobs are batch ETL, not low-latency request handlers.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/welcome.html

data store will continue to grow and will be petabytes in size. The company needs to build a highly available data ingestion solution that facilitates
on-demand analytics of existing data and new data with SQL.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
correctAnswer: Send activity data to an Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream. Configure the stream to deliver the data to an Amazon Redshift cluster.
incorrectAnswers: Send activity data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Configure the stream to deliver the data to an Amazon S3 bucket.
Place activity data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure Amazon S3 to run an AWS Lambda function on the data as the data arrives in the S3 bucket.
Create an ingestion service on Amazon EC2 instances that are spread across multiple Availability Zones. Configure the service to forward data to an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ database.
explanation:
Amazon Data Firehose is fully managed and delivers streaming data to Amazon Redshift (via S3 and COPY), which supports on-demand SQL analytics at petabyte scale. Kinesis Data Streams requires you to build consumers, and RDS does not scale to petabytes.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/what-is-this-service.html

question:
A company needs to retain its AWS CloudTrail logs for 3 years. The company is enforcing CloudTrail across a set of AWS accounts by using AWS
Organizations from the parent account. The CloudTrail target S3 bucket is configured with S3 Versioning enabled. An S3 Lifecycle policy is in
place to delete current objects after 3 years.
After the fourth year of use of the S3 bucket, the S3 bucket metrics show that the number of objects has continued to rise. However, the number
of new CloudTrail logs that are delivered to the S3 bucket has remained consistent.
Which solution will delete objects that are older than 3 years in the MOST cost-effective manner?
correctAnswer: Configure the S3 Lifecycle policy to delete previous versions as well as current versions.
incorrectAnswers: Configure the organization’s centralized CloudTrail trail to expire objects after 3 years.
Create an AWS Lambda function to enumerate and delete objects from Amazon S3 that are older than 3 years.
Configure the parent account as the owner of all objects that are delivered to the S3 bucket.
explanation:
In a versioned bucket the Expiration action only creates a delete marker and keeps the old version as noncurrent. Adding a NoncurrentVersionExpiration action permanently deletes those versions at no extra cost, whereas a Lambda function adds cost and CloudTrail has no expiry setting.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/intro-lifecycle-rules.html

factChecks.explanation: With versioning, the Expiration action only adds delete markers to current versions; noncurrent versions remain, so object count grows. Fix is to also expire noncurrent versions via the lifecycle policy. Key (trail setting) is not a real option; explanation generic.

A company has an API that receives real-time data from a fleet of monitoring devices. The API stores this data in an Amazon RDS DB instance for
later analysis. The amount of data that the monitoring devices send to the API fluctuates. During periods of heavy traffic, the API often returns
timeout errors.
After an inspection of the logs, the company determines that the database is not capable of processing the volume of write traffic that comes
from the API. A solutions architect must minimize the number of connections to the database and must ensure that data is not lost during periods
of heavy traffic.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Modify the API to write incoming data to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use an AWS Lambda function that Amazon SQS invokes to write data from the queue to the database.
incorrectAnswers: Increase the size of the DB instance to an instance type that has more available memory.
Modify the DB instance to be a Multi-AZ DB instance. Configure the application to write to all active RDS DB instances.
Modify the API to write incoming data to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Use an AWS Lambda function that Amazon SNS invokes to write data from the topic to the database.
explanation:
SQS durably queues the bursts and Lambda event source mapping batches messages and can limit concurrency, so far fewer database connections are used and no data is lost. A bigger instance does not reduce connections, Multi-AZ standby cannot accept writes, and SNS pushes immediately so it does not smooth the load.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html

factChecks.explanation: Scaling up the DB instance does not reduce connections nor guarantee no data loss. Buffering writes in SQS and having a Lambda function consume from the queue (with batching/limited concurrency) reduces connection count and prevents loss. SNS does not retain messages for slow consumers the same way and the standard answer is SQS.

incorrectAnswers: Use Auto Scaling groups with Network Load Balancers for the NAT instances in different Availability Zones.

incorrectAnswers: Create a DB instance security group that allows all traffic from the public IP address of the application server in VPC A.

incorrectAnswers: Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) certificates on the ALB to encrypt data in transit. Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to encrypt the EBS volumes and Aurora database storage at rest.

A company is moving its on-premises Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. The database has several applications that write to the
same tables. The applications need to be migrated one by one with a month in between each migration. Management has expressed concerns
that the database has a high number of reads and writes. The data must be kept in sync across both databases throughout the migration.
What should a solutions architect recommend?
correctAnswer: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool with AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) using a memory optimized replication instance. Create a full load plus change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select all tables.
incorrectAnswers: Use AWS DataSync for the initial migration. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create a change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select all tables.

Use AWS DataSync for the initial migration. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create a full load plus change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select all tables.

Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool with AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) using a compute optimized replication instance. Create a full load plus change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select the largest tables.
explanation:

question:
A company runs a web application that is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances in the private subnet of a VPC. An Application Load Balancer (ALB)
that extends across the public subnets directs web traffic to the EC2 instances. The company wants to implement new security measures to
restrict inbound traffic from the ALB to the EC2 instances while preventing access from any other source inside or outside the private subnet of
the EC2 instances.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Configure the security group for the EC2 instances to only allow traffic that comes from the security group for the ALB.
incorrectAnswers: Configure a route in a route table to direct traffic from the internet to the private IP addresses of the EC2 instances.
Move the EC2 instances into the public subnet. Give the EC2 instances a set of Elastic IP addresses.
Configure the security group for the ALB to allow any TCP traffic on any port.
explanation:
To ensure targets receive traffic only from the load balancer, set the ALB security group as the source in the target security group's ingress rule. Routing internet traffic to the instances or moving them to a public subnet exposes them instead.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-update-security-groups.html

factChecks.explanation: Keyed answer (route internet traffic to private IPs) is nonsense and does the opposite. Correct: allow only the ALB security group as source in the instance security group.

question:
A research company runs experiments that are powered by a simulation application and a visualization application. The simulation application
runs on Linux and outputs intermediate data to an NFS share every 5 minutes. The visualization application is a Windows desktop application that
displays the simulation output and requires an SMB file system.
The company maintains two synchronized file systems. This strategy is causing data duplication and inefficient resource usage. The company
needs to migrate the applications to AWS without making code changes to either application.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Migrate the simulation application to Linux Amazon EC2 instances. Migrate the visualization application to Windows EC2 instances. Configure Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP for storage.
incorrectAnswers: Migrate both applications to AWS Lambda. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to exchange data between the applications.
Migrate both applications to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Configure shared storage with Amazon S3.

Migrate the simulation application to Linux Amazon EC2 instances. Migrate the visualization application to Windows EC2 instances. Configure Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to exchange data between the applications.
explanation:
FSx for NetApp ONTAP offers multi-protocol access (NFS and SMB) to a single copy of data, so both unchanged applications can share one file system. Lambda/S3 and SQS would require code changes.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/ONTAPGuide/what-is-fsx-ontap.html

question:
A company hosts its static website by using Amazon S3. The company wants to add a contact form to its webpage. The contact form will have
dynamic server-side components for users to input their name, email address, phone number, and user message. The company anticipates that
there will be fewer than 100 site visits each month.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
correctAnswer: Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint with an AWS Lambda backend that makes a call to Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).
incorrectAnswers: Host a dynamic contact form page in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Set up Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to connect to any third-party email provider.
Convert the static webpage to dynamic by deploying Amazon Lightsail. Use client-side scripting to build the contact form. Integrate the form with Amazon WorkMail.

Create a t2.micro Amazon EC2 instance. Deploy a LAMP (Linux, Apache, MySQL, PHP/Perl/Python) stack to host the webpage. Use client-side scripting to build the contact form. Integrate the form with Amazon WorkMail.
explanation:
With API Gateway and Lambda you pay only per request, so at fewer than 100 visits per month the cost is close to zero, and Lambda can send the form contents through SES. ECS, Lightsail and EC2 all bill for always-running capacity.

Source: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/architecture/create-dynamic-contact-forms-for-s3-static-websites-using-aws-lambda-amazon-api-gateway-and-amazon-ses/

factChecks.explanation: Keyed ECS-hosted page is not the most cost-effective option for under 100 visits/month (always-on tasks), and SES does not 'connect to a third-party email provider'. API Gateway + Lambda + SES is the serverless pay-per-request answer AWS documents for S3 static-site contact forms. Explanation describes EBS, unrelated.

question:
A company has a static website that is hosted on Amazon CloudFront in front of Amazon S3. The static website uses a database backend. The
company notices that the website does not reflect updates that have been made in the website’s Git repository. The company checks the
continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipeline between the Git repository and Amazon S3. The company verifies that the
webhooks are configured properly and that the CI/CD pipeline is sending messages that indicate successful deployments.
A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that displays the updates on the website.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Invalidate the CloudFront cache.
incorrectAnswers: Add an Application Load Balancer.
Add Amazon ElastiCache for Redis or Memcached to the database layer of the web application.
Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to validate the website's SSL certificate.
explanation:
CloudFront serves cached copies until they expire; invalidating the cache makes edge locations fetch the latest files from S3. An ALB, a database cache, or certificate validation do not refresh cached static content.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/Invalidation.html

factChecks.explanation: Stale content served from CloudFront edge caches is fixed by invalidating the cache; adding an ALB does nothing. Question text is also odd (static site with database backend).

question:
A company wants to migrate a Windows-based application from on premises to the AWS Cloud. The application has three tiers: an application tier,
a business tier, and a database tier with Microsoft SQL Server. The company wants to use specific features of SQL Server such as native backups
and Data Quality Services. The company also needs to share files for processing between the tiers.
How should a solutions architect design the architecture to meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server for file sharing between the tiers.
incorrectAnswers: Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx File Gateway for file sharing between the tiers.
Host the application tier and the business tier on Amazon EC2 instances. Host the database tier on Amazon RDS. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) for file sharing between the tiers.

Host the application tier and the business tier on Amazon EC2 instances. Host the database tier on Amazon RDS. Use a Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume for file sharing between the tiers.
explanation:
RDS for SQL Server does not support Data Quality Services, so SQL Server must run on EC2. FSx for Windows File Server provides managed SMB shares for Windows tiers. FSx File Gateway is an on-premises cache for FSx and is no longer offered to new customers.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/filefsxw/what-is-file-fsxw.html

factChecks.explanation: Key is wrong and outdated: Amazon FSx File Gateway is for on-premises access to FSx and is no longer available to new customers. Native SQL Server backups/Data Quality Services require SQL Server on EC2; shared Windows files between tiers use FSx for Windows File Server.

question:
A company is migrating a Linux-based web server group to AWS. The web servers must access files in a shared file store for some content. The
company must not make any changes to the application.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system on all web servers.
incorrectAnswers: Create an Amazon S3 Standard bucket with access to the web servers.
Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an Amazon S3 bucket as the origin.
Configure a General Purpose SSD (gp3) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Mount the EBS volume to all web servers.
explanation:
EFS provides a shared NFS file system that many Linux instances can mount concurrently, so the application needs no changes. S3 and CloudFront are object/API based, and a standard EBS volume cannot be mounted by multiple servers across AZs.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/whatisefs.html

factChecks.explanation: An S3 bucket is object storage and would require application changes; the requirement is a shared file store for Linux web servers with no application change, i.e. Amazon EFS mounted on all servers (NFS/POSIX).

question:
A company has an AWS Lambda function that needs read access to an Amazon S3 bucket that is located in the same AWS account.
Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure manner?
correctAnswer: Apply an IAM role to the Lambda function. Apply an IAM policy to the role to grant read access to the S3 bucket.
incorrectAnswers: Apply an S3 bucket policy that grants read access to the S3 bucket.
Embed an access key and a secret key in the Lambda function's code to grant the required IAM permissions for read access to the S3 bucket.
Apply an IAM role to the Lambda function. Apply an IAM policy to the role to grant read access to all S3 buckets in the account.
explanation:
Lambda assumes its execution role automatically and receives temporary credentials, and scoping the policy to the one bucket follows least privilege. Hard-coded keys are insecure, and granting read to all buckets is over-permissive.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-intro-execution-role.html

factChecks.explanation: A bucket policy alone does not give the Lambda function credentials (it still needs an execution role) and as worded names no principal. The most secure approach is an IAM execution role with a policy scoped to read only that bucket (least privilege); embedding keys or granting all buckets is worse.

question:
A company hosts a web application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling group that scales in response to
user demand. The company wants to optimize cost savings without making a long-term commitment.
Which EC2 instance purchasing option should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: A mix of On-Demand Instances and Spot Instances
incorrectAnswers: Dedicated Instances only
On-Demand Instances only
A mix of On-Demand Instances and Reserved Instances
explanation:
Reserved Instances require a 1- or 3-year commitment; Dedicated Instances add cost. A mixed instances policy with On-Demand base capacity and Spot for scaling optimizes cost without commitment.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-mixed-instances-groups.html

factChecks.explanation: Keyed answer 'Dedicated Instances only' is wrong: Dedicated Instances cost more. With no long-term commitment, Spot plus On-Demand in the ASG optimizes cost. The explanation's own doc quote supports Spot plus On-Demand.

question:
A company has an on-premises volume backup solution that has reached its end of life. The company wants to use AWS as part of a new backup
solution and wants to maintain local access to all the data while it is backed up on AWS. The company wants to ensure that the data backed up on
AWS is automatically and securely transferred.
Which solution meets these requirements?
correctAnswer: Use AWS Storage Gateway and configure a stored volume gateway. Run the Storage Gateway software appliance on premises and map the gateway storage volumes to on-premises storage. Mount the gateway storage volumes to provide local access to the data.
incorrectAnswers: Use AWS Snowball to migrate data out of the on-premises solution to Amazon S3. Configure on-premises systems to mount the Snowball S3 endpoint to provide local access to the data.
Use AWS Snowball Edge to migrate data out of the on-premises solution to Amazon S3. Use the Snowball Edge file interface to provide on-premises systems with local access to the data.

Use AWS Storage Gateway and configure a cached volume gateway. Run the Storage Gateway software appliance on premises and configure a percentage of data to cache locally. Mount the gateway storage volumes to provide local access to the data.
explanation:
Stored volumes keep the full dataset on local storage for low-latency access while asynchronously backing it up to S3 as EBS snapshots over an encrypted connection. Cached volumes keep only frequently accessed data locally, so they do not provide local access to all data.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/storagegateway/latest/vgw/StorageGatewayConcepts.html

factChecks.explanation: Requirement: keep local access to all data while backed up to AWS automatically. Stored volume gateway keeps the entire dataset on premises with async backup to S3. Cached volumes keep only hot data locally; Snowball is not an automatic ongoing backup. Ligature loss in options.

question:
An application that is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances needs to access an Amazon S3 bucket. Traffic must not traverse the internet.
How should a solutions architect configure access to meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Set up a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC.
incorrectAnswers: Create a private hosted zone by using Amazon Route 53.
Configure the EC2 instances to use a NAT gateway to access the S3 bucket.
Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the VPC and the S3 bucket.
explanation:
A gateway VPC endpoint routes EC2-to-S3 traffic over the AWS network without an internet gateway or NAT. A private hosted zone only handles DNS, a NAT gateway uses the internet path, and a VPN cannot terminate at S3.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/privatelink-interface-endpoints.html

factChecks.explanation: Key (Route 53 private hosted zone) does not keep S3 traffic off the internet; a gateway VPC endpoint for S3 does.

question:
A development team has launched a new application that is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances inside a development VPC. A solutions architect
needs to create a new VPC in the same account. The new VPC will be peered with the development VPC. The VPC CIDR block for the development
VPC is 192.168.0.0/24. The solutions architect needs to create a CIDR block for the new VPC. The CIDR block must be valid for a VPC peering
connection to the development VPC.
What is the SMALLEST CIDR block that meets these requirements?
explanation:
VPC peering requires non-overlapping CIDRs and VPC CIDR blocks must be /16 through /28. 192.168.0.0/24 overlaps the development VPC and /32 blocks are not valid VPC sizes, leaving 10.0.1.0/24.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-cidr-blocks.html

factChecks.explanation: VPC CIDR blocks must be between /16 and /28, so /32 is invalid. 192.168.0.0/24 overlaps the dev VPC (peering requires non-overlapping CIDRs). Only 10.0.1.0/24 is valid and non-overlapping.

question:
A company deploys an application on five Amazon EC2 instances. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) distributes traffic to the instances by using
a target group. The average CPU usage on each of the instances is below 10% most of the time, with occasional surges to 65%.
A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to automate the scalability of the application. The solution must optimize the cost of the
architecture and must ensure that the application has enough CPU resources when surges occur.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Select the existing ALB as the load balancer and the existing target group as the target group. Set a target tracking scaling policy that is based on the ASGAverageCPUUtilization metric. Set the minimum instances to 2, the desired capacity to 3, the maximum instances to 6, and the target value to 50%. Add the EC2 instances to the Auto Scaling group.
incorrectAnswers: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that enters the ALARM state when the CPUUtilization metric is less than 20%. Create an AWS Lambda function that the CloudWatch alarm invokes to terminate one of the EC2 instances in the ALB target group.

Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Select the existing ALB as the load balancer and the existing target group as the target group. Set the minimum instances to 2, the desired capacity to 3, and the maximum instances to 6. Add the EC2 instances to the Auto Scaling group.

Create two Amazon CloudWatch alarms. Configure the first CloudWatch alarm to enter the ALARM state when the average CPUUtilization metric is below 20%. Configure the second CloudWatch alarm to enter the ALARM state when the average CPUUtilization metric is above 50%. Configure the alarms to publish to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send an email message. After receiving the message, log in to decrease or increase the number of EC2 instances that are running.
explanation:
Target tracking on average CPU automatically adds instances during surges and removes them when idle, optimizing cost; an ASG without a scaling policy does not react to load, and manual or terminate-only approaches cannot guarantee capacity.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-scaling-target-tracking.html

factChecks.explanation: Key is wrong: a Lambda that only terminates instances cannot add capacity during surges. Correct answer is an Auto Scaling group with a target tracking policy on ASGAverageCPUUtilization. Typos in options: 'trafficking' should be 'tracking', 'matric' should be 'metric'.

question:
A company is running a critical business application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The EC2 instances run in an
Auto Scaling group and access an Amazon RDS DB instance.
The design did not pass an operational review because the EC2 instances and the DB instance are all located in a single Availability Zone. A
solutions architect must update the design to use a second Availability Zone.
Which solution will make the application highly available?
correctAnswer: Provision a subnet in each Availability Zone. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance for Multi-AZ deployment.
incorrectAnswers: Provision a subnet in each Availability Zone. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance with connections to each network.

Provision two subnets that extend across both Availability Zones. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance with connections to each network.

Provision a subnet that extends across both Availability Zones. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance for Multi-AZ deployment.
explanation:
A subnet exists in a single AZ, so one subnet per AZ lets the Auto Scaling group span both zones, and Multi-AZ gives the RDS instance an automatic-failover standby. Subnets cannot extend across AZs.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZ.html

factChecks.explanation: RDS high availability requires Multi-AZ deployment; 'connections to each network' is not a thing. Also subnets cannot span AZs, so one subnet per AZ is required.

question:
A research laboratory needs to process approximately 8 TB of data. The laboratory requires sub-millisecond latencies and a minimum throughput
of 6 GBps for the storage subsystem. Hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances that run Amazon Linux will distribute and process the data.
Which solution will meet the performance requirements?
correctAnswer: Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the raw data. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system that uses persistent SSD storage. Select the option to import data from and export data to Amazon S3. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.
incorrectAnswers: Create an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system. Set each volume's tiering policy to ALL. Import the raw data into the file system. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.

Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the raw data. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system that uses persistent HDD storage. Select the option to import data from and export data to Amazon S3. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.
Create an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system. Set each volume's tiering policy to NONE. Import the raw data into the file system. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.
explanation:
The FSx for Lustre SSD storage class provides consistent sub-millisecond latency and very high throughput for hundreds of Linux clients, with S3 integration. HDD storage gives single-digit ms latency, and ONTAP with tiering ALL keeps data in the slower capacity pool.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/what-is.html

factChecks.explanation: Key (FSx for ONTAP with tiering ALL) pushes data to the capacity pool, which cannot give sub-millisecond latency. FSx for Lustre (SSD) is the HPC fit with sub-ms latency and S3 integration. Key text also has typos ('Sat', 'la').

question:
A company needs to migrate a legacy application from an on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud because of hardware capacity constraints.
The application runs 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. The application’s database storage continues to grow over time.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
correctAnswer: Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon Aurora Reserved Instances.
incorrectAnswers: Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon S3.
Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon RDS On-Demand Instances.
Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon RDS Reserved Instances.
explanation:
A workload running 24/7 benefits from Reserved Instance discounts on both tiers, and Aurora storage grows automatically as data grows. Spot can be interrupted and S3 is not a drop-in database for a legacy application.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Overview.StorageReliability.html

factChecks.explanation: Spot Instances and S3 as a replacement for a legacy relational database do not fit a 24/7 legacy app. Reserved Instances for the app and Aurora Reserved Instances (storage auto-grows) is the most cost-effective.

question:
A university research laboratory needs to migrate 30 TB of data from an on-premises Windows file server to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server.
The laboratory has a 1 Gbps network link that many other departments in the university share.
The laboratory wants to implement a data migration service that will maximize the performance of the data transfer. However, the laboratory
needs to be able to control the amount of bandwidth that the service uses to minimize the impact on other departments. The data migration must
take place within the next 5 days.
Which AWS solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: AWS DataSync
incorrectAnswers: AWS Snowcone
Amazon FSx File Gateway
AWS Transfer Family
explanation:
DataSync is an accelerated transfer service that can target FSx for Windows File Server and lets you throttle bandwidth per task or execution. Snowcone is too small and Transfer Family does not migrate SMB shares to FSx.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/configure-bandwidth.html

factChecks.explanation: Snowcone (8/14 TB) cannot hold 30 TB and cannot load directly into FSx. AWS DataSync supports FSx for Windows as a destination and lets you set a bandwidth limit. FSx File Gateway is also not a migration service.

question:
A company is launching a new application deployed on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster and is using the Fargate
launch type for ECS tasks. The company is monitoring CPU and memory usage because it is expecting high traffic to the application upon its
launch. However, the company wants to reduce costs when utilization decreases.
What should a solutions architect recommend?
correctAnswer: Use AWS Application Auto Scaling with target tracking policies to scale when ECS metric breaches trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.
incorrectAnswers: Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling to scale at certain periods based on previous traffic patterns.
Use an AWS Lambda function to scale Amazon ECS based on metric breaches that trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.
Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling with simple scaling policies to scale when ECS metric breaches trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.

A company is hosting a three-tier ecommerce application in the AWS Cloud. The company hosts the website on Amazon S3 and integrates the
website with an API that handles sales requests. The company hosts the API on three Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load
Balancer (ALB). The API consists of static and dynamic front-end content along with backend workers that process sales requests
asynchronously.
The company is expecting a significant and sudden increase in the number of sales requests during events for the launch of new products.
What should a solutions architect recommend to ensure that all the requests are processed successfully?
correctAnswer: Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the static content. Add an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to receive requests from the website for later processing by the EC2 instances.
incorrectAnswers: Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the dynamic content. Increase the number of EC2 instances to handle the increase in traffic.
Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the static content. Place the EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group to launch new instances based on network traffic.
Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the dynamic content. Add an Amazon ElastiCache instance in front of the ALB to reduce traffic for the API to handle.
explanation:
An SQS queue buffers the asynchronous sales requests so none are lost when traffic spikes, while CloudFront offloads static content. Manually adding instances or scaling on network traffic does not guarantee every request is eventually processed.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html

factChecks.explanation: To ensure ALL requests are processed during sudden spikes, the key is decoupling the asynchronous sales requests with an SQS queue; the keyed answer only scales manually (increasing instance count by hand) and does not guarantee processing.

regular security scans across a large fleet of EC2 instances. The solution should also patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule and provide a
report of each instance’s patch status.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
correctAnswer: Turn on Amazon Inspector in the account. Configure Amazon Inspector to scan the EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities. Set up AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule.
incorrectAnswers: Set up Amazon Macie to scan the EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities. Set up a cron job on each EC2 instance to patch the instance on a regular schedule.

Turn on Amazon GuardDuty in the account. Configure GuardDuty to scan the EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities. Set up AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule.
Set up Amazon Detective to scan the EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities. Set up an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule.
explanation:
Amazon Inspector continually scans EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities, and Patch Manager patches on a schedule and reports patch status. Macie, GuardDuty, and Detective do not scan instances for vulnerabilities.

Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/inspector/latest/user/what-is-inspector.html
